subsystems.name: Code lattice
subsystems.role: the geometry that defines which qubits exist and which stabilisers are measured.

subsystems.name: Physical qubit layer
subsystems.role: the hardware holding the data and ancilla qubits.
parts: superconducting transmons, trapped ions or neutral atoms

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction
subsystems.role: measures each stabiliser without collapsing the encoded information.
parts: flag qubits to catch ancilla faults

subsystems.name: Classical decoder
subsystems.role: reads the error syndromes and infers the most likely correction.

subsystems.name: Logical gate layer
parts: lattice surgery or code switching for entangling gates

buildSteps.title: Pick the tiling and distance
buildSteps.detail: Choose a three-colourable lattice and code distance d; the number of physical qubits and the weight-6 face stabilisers follow from it.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the qubits
buildSteps.detail: Assign data qubits to vertices and ancillas to stabiliser measurements, then map that graph onto the fixed connectivity of the hardware.

buildSteps.title: Schedule the entangling gates
buildSteps.detail: Break each high-weight stabiliser into a sequence of two-qubit gates, adding flag qubits so a single ancilla fault cannot masquerade as a data error.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate syndrome extraction
buildSteps.detail: Tune gate timings and readout so one round of measurement is fast, low-noise and repeatable.

buildSteps.title: Build and train the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Implement a decoder that handles the heavier, more tangled error patterns of a colour code, ideally running within the measurement cycle.

buildSteps.title: Verify below-threshold behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Run increasing distances and confirm that logical error rate falls as the code grows — the only real proof the code is working.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate the transversal gates
buildSteps.detail: Apply Hadamard and phase gates qubit-by-qubit across the block and check that logical information survives with no error spreading.

buildSteps.title: Add non-Clifford capability
buildSteps.detail: Distil or inject magic states so the processor can run arbitrary algorithms, not just Clifford circuits.

buildSteps.title: Scale out
buildSteps.detail: Combine blocks by lattice surgery or code switching to link many logical qubits into one machine.

prerequisites.tech: Physical qubits with error rates near or below the code threshold
prerequisites.why: if physical error rates exceed threshold, adding qubits makes the logical qubit worse, not better.

prerequisites.tech: High-fidelity two-qubit gates and mid-circuit measurement
prerequisites.why: syndrome extraction is built entirely from these two operations.
the decoder must keep up with measurement, and colour codes are harder to decode than surface codes.
colour codes check six qubits at once, so a single ancilla fault can create a damaging correlated error.
a transversal gate set alone is not universal; a non-Clifford resource is needed for useful computation.
the lattice rarely matches hardware wiring, so qubits must be shuttled or swapped without adding errors.

pathway.milestone: theory mature since Bombin and Martin-Delgado introduced colour codes in 2006; small-distance versions run on a handful of qubits
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the lattice and gate scheme are self-consistent.

pathway.milestone: distance-3 to distance-5 logical qubits showing error suppression with real-time decoding
pathway.unlocks: evidence that colour codes are competitive with surface codes on real hardware.

pathway.milestone: end-to-end demonstration of the transversal Clifford gate set plus magic-state injection
pathway.unlocks: a genuinely universal, fault-tolerant logical gate layer.

pathway.milestone: code switching between colour and surface codes inside one processor
pathway.unlocks: cheap transversal gates where they help, and cheaper storage and layout where they do not.
